name: Light Cyan
lede: Light Cyan is a very pale aqua tint, a CSS and X11 keyword whose parent word, cyan, is a primary of printing.

notes.cite: Eckstut & Eckstut, What Is Color?, Q. 35 (What Is Subtractive Color?)
ColorHub library (data/library.json): sources CSS, Wikipedia, xkcd (alt #ACFFFC); CIEDE2000
ColorHub archive field notes for Light Cyan (n=7), 23,781 museum paintings as photographed; data/graph/fieldnotes/l.json

sections.title: A tint of a primary
sections.body: Paterson lists LightCyan as an X11 color with the hex code E0FFFF [1]. Cyan itself he defines as a greenish blue and one of the three subtractive primary colours [1]. Eckstut and Eckstut explain that cyan pigment takes red out of white light and sends back blue and green, which is why cyan, not blue, is a printer's primary [2]. Light Cyan is that hue thinned almost to white [3].

sections.title: On the list
sections.body: The library finds the swatch in CSS, Wikipedia and the xkcd survey, whose own light cyan is a stronger, greener #ACFFFC [3]. The nearest everyday name is [[powder-blue]], about eight units away; other close names are [[aqua]], [[azure]] and [[alice-blue]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is rare in museum paintings: 7 of 23,781 contain it, about 0.03 per cent [4]. The earliest dated painting is from 1872, by Ricardo Maria Navarrete Fos, and the latest from 1905 [4]. In printed English the phrase's word peaks in the 2000s, though that count covers every sense [4].
